identity.title: Emergency Action Plan – Portland Facility
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is the company's own written emergency action plan for the Portland facility. It is the company's document, so the company has to keep it complete and up to date. Oregon OSHA requires it under OAR 437-002-0042 because the site has more than 10 employees. It covers alarms, evacuation routes, shelter-in-place, headcounts, first aid and training. However, several elements the rule requires are missing, including how to report an emergency, how to shut down critical equipment, and names or job titles of contacts. The appendices it depends on (maps and roster) are not in this file. The plan was last revised in February 2021 and nothing shows the yearly January review it promises.
scan.freshness_note: The cover page (page 1) says 'Revised February 2021'. Only the month is given, so I used the 1st as the date. That is more than five and a half years ago. Section 6 promises a review every January, but nothing in the file records one. Ask the facilities lead whether a newer version or a review log exists. If not, a revision is overdue.

gaps.title: No procedure for reporting a fire or other emergency
gaps.description: The plan mentions pull stations (Section 2) and says emergency medical services are called for serious injuries (Section 5). It never tells employees how to report a fire, chemical release or other emergency: who calls 911, from which phone, and what to tell the dispatcher, including the fact that the building stores chemicals.
gaps.fix: Add a short 'Reporting an emergency' section. Say to pull the nearest station and call 911, and name the job title responsible for calling 911 and briefing the fire department about the chemicals on site. Also say how to report an emergency when the alarm is not involved, such as a medical call or a small spill.
gaps.locator: not in the document (would fit after Section 2)
gaps.quote: Manual pull stations are located at each exit door.

gaps.title: No procedure for shutting down critical equipment before evacuating
gaps.description: Employees are told to 'secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds'. The plan never says which equipment needs to be shut down, if any, or who does it. That could include lab processes, transfer or dispensing pumps, forklift charging, gas cylinders or heating. The only shutdown described is the ventilation shutdown during shelter-in-place.
gaps.fix: List any equipment that should be shut down or kept running during an evacuation, and give the job title responsible for each. If none needs to be, say so in writing.
gaps.quote: all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit

gaps.title: No names or job titles of people to contact about the plan
gaps.description: The plan does not name anyone, by name or job title, whom employees can ask about the plan or their duties under it. The roles it mentions ('facilities lead', 'receptionist', 'incident coordinator') are not given as contacts.
gaps.fix: Add a contacts section. Give the name or job title of the plan owner, and of the person or people who can explain the plan and duties under it, with phone numbers.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-002-0042(2). This matches the federal 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(6). I confirmed that Oregon subsections (a) to (d) exist but did not confirm which letter covers this element. I believe it is (f).
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January

gaps.title: Incident coordinator role never assigned
gaps.description: Section 4 depends on an 'incident coordinator' who takes the headcount results, briefs the fire department and gives the all-clear. The plan never says which person or job title fills that role, or who backs them up on each shift.
gaps.fix: Name the job title of the incident coordinator and an alternate for each shift, and add them to the roster.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-002-0042(2)(b) (procedures to account for all employees). Applying it to this role is my own reading.
gaps.quote: Any person unaccounted for is reported at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point

gaps.title: Appendices A and B not in the file
gaps.description: The exit route assignments and the warden and first-aid roster are said to be in Appendix A (evacuation maps) and Appendix B (roster). Only the titles of the appendices appear on page 5. The maps and roster themselves are not attached, so this copy of the plan cannot show exit route assignments or who the wardens are.
gaps.fix: Attach the current evacuation maps and a dated roster to the plan, and upload them here.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-002-0042(2)(a) (procedures for emergency evacuation, including exit route assignments)
gaps.quote: Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)

gaps.title: Earthquake named in scope but no earthquake procedure
gaps.description: Section 1 lists earthquake as an emergency the plan covers. The plan only gives procedures for alarm-triggered evacuation and shelter-in-place. It does not say what to do during shaking (drop, cover, hold on; stay away from racking) or afterwards (checking for chemical spills and container damage before re-entering).
gaps.fix: Add an earthquake section covering what to do during shaking, when to evacuate afterwards, and who checks racking and chemical storage before anyone goes back in.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-002-0042(2)(a) (procedures for emergency evacuation, including type of evacuation). This is my reading. The rule does not name earthquakes.
gaps.locator: Section 1 names it; no procedure anywhere in the document
gaps.quote: a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility

gaps.title: No instructions for a chemical spill or release inside the building
gaps.description: The plan covers an outdoor chemical release (shelter-in-place) and a person exposed to a chemical. It does not say what employees do when a product spills or leaks inside the warehouse, dock or lab. It does not say whether staff clean up small spills or everyone evacuates, or who decides. For a chemical distributor, this is the most likely emergency.
gaps.fix: Add an indoor spill section. Say which small spills trained staff may clean up, and with what kit and protective equipment. Say that anything larger means evacuating and calling 911. If employees are not expected to respond to releases, say so in writing.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.120(q)(1)–(2). I believe Oregon adopts this by reference in Division 2, Subdivision H, but I did not check that. Employers who evacuate employees and do not let them respond may fall under the emergency action plan exemption in (q)(1).
gaps.locator: not in the document (would fit in Section 3 or as a new section)
gaps.quote: For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place signal sounds.

gaps.title: Silent on who may use fire extinguishers
gaps.description: The plan does not say whether employees are expected to fight small fires with portable extinguishers or just evacuate. That choice decides which extinguisher training and equipment rules apply.
gaps.fix: State the policy. Either everyone evacuates and no one uses extinguishers, or named trained employees may fight small fires. Then match the training records to that choice.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.157(a)–(b) (portable fire extinguishers), adopted in Oregon Division 2, Subdivision L. I did not confirm the exact Oregon rule number.

gaps.title: No record that the promised January reviews happened
gaps.description: Section 6 promises a review by the facilities lead every January. The plan still carries its February 2021 revision date, and it has no review log or sign-off, so there is no record of the January 2022–2026 reviews.
gaps.fix: Add a review log to the plan (date, reviewer, changes made), carry out a review now, and update the revision date.
gaps.citation: null (this is the plan's own commitment, not a specific rule)
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January

deadlines.source_line: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead.

deadlines.source_line: Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.

deadlines.source_line: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January

deadlines.source_line: Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually.

facts.quote: It applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility
facts.affects: More than 10 employees means the plan must be in writing under OAR 437-002-0042(1)(b). The count may have changed since 2021.

facts.value: Warehouse, delivery drivers, laboratory and office staff; loading dock
facts.quote: including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff
facts.affects: A lab and chemical warehousing bring in hazard communication, lab chemical rules and spill response.

facts.value: Monitored 24/7 by Cascade Fire & Safety under a service contract; horns and strobes; pull stations at each exit; tested monthly
facts.quote: The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety under a service contract.
facts.affects: Covers the plan's alarm-system element. Monitoring contracts and test records should be on file.

facts.value: Emergency shower and eyewash at the loading dock
facts.quote: taken to the emergency shower and eyewash at the loading dock
facts.affects: Eyewash and shower rules apply. Whether the lab and warehouse corrosives areas are close enough to a unit is unverified.

facts.value: More than one shift is likely
facts.quote: two per shift, named on the warden roster
facts.affects: Wardens, first-aid responders and an incident coordinator are needed on every shift.

scan.confidence_notes: The document was fully readable (5 pages). I checked the required elements (a) to (d) of OAR 437-002-0042(2) against the Oregon Secretary of State rule text. I did not confirm which Oregon subsection covers names or job titles of contacts. I also did not confirm the Oregon rule numbers under which Oregon adopts the hazardous waste operations and emergency response rule (HAZWOPER, 29 CFR 1910.120) and the portable fire extinguisher rule (29 CFR 1910.157). The earthquake, incident coordinator and indoor spill findings are my interpretation, not explicit rule wording. The revision date gives only the month, so I used the 1st. Facts date from 2021 and may be out of date.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
